inputValidationNote: API-level range bounds (in the Flask service) are the observedTrainingRange values above, padded 5% and clipped at 0 where negative is meaningless. These represent the range the model has training evidence for, NOT physical/industry engineering limits.
preprocessing: sklearn ColumnTransformer: StandardScaler on 5 numeric features, OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown=ignore) on Type. Fit only on training split, bundled inside the serialized Pipeline.

dataset.name: AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset
dataset.nature: Public benchmark dataset. Explicitly synthetic/simulated - NOT real industrial telemetry.

droppedColumns.leakageReason: These are components of the target definition (failure sub-modes whose logical OR determines Machine failure in 99.73% of rows) and are not available as legitimate pre-failure input at inference time.

predictionSemantics: Point-in-time failure-state risk score for the observed operating snapshot, as labeled in AI4I 2020. The dataset does not encode a future time window, so this is NOT a 'probability of failure within N days/hours' claim.

trainingConfig.splitProtocol: stratified 60/20/20 (train/val/test), two sequential train_test_split calls, random_state=42

modelSelection.selectionMetric: validation PR-AUC (accuracy not used - target is 96.6% negative class)

validationMetrics_threshold_0.5.note: Unaffected by the shared-preprocessor bug below - computed immediately after fit, before any other pipeline touched the preprocessor.

calibration.conclusion: Both calibration methods increased Brier score (worse). Model kept UNCALIBRATED. Application must present output as 'risk score', not 'calibrated probability'.

orderAwareRobustnessCheck.note: UDI is a documented row identifier, not a timestamp; rows are independent simulated snapshots. This is a distribution-shift robustness check, NOT a temporal leakage test.
orderAwareRobustnessCheck.interpretation: Performance degrades under UDI-ordered split by more than class-balance differences alone would predict. Reported as an open, unresolved finding - not claimed as proof of temporal dependency, not dismissed either.

thresholdPolicy.costAssumption: False negative (missed failure) assumed 5x costlier than false positive (false alarm). Explicit modeling assumption, NOT a sourced business/industry figure.
tieBreakRule: 2. among cost ties, choose higher recall
3. among remaining ties, choose higher threshold

selectedOperatingPoint.note: The project selected ONE operating point (5:1 assumption) as the active serving policy. This is a binary decision (below/at-or-above threshold), NOT a three-level LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH scheme. The 0.57 value above came from a different, mutually exclusive cost assumption (1:1/2:1) and is retained in sensitivityTable for transparency only - it is not used to classify risk. No experiment has validated combining 0.03 and 0.57 into a single three-tier policy; that would require its own study before being implemented.

permutationImportance.note: Sanity check only - NOT a causal claim. Method: sklearn permutation_importance, scoring=average_precision, n_repeats=20, on canonical validation set.

reproducibilityBugFixed: An earlier draft shared one ColumnTransformer instance by reference across multiple Pipeline objects (official model, order-aware experiment, calibration). Fitting a later pipeline silently overwrote the earlier one's learned scaler statistics, corrupting the test-set numbers computed after that point. Fixed by giving every pipeline its own freshly-constructed ColumnTransformer. Verified via assertion that refitting reproduces byte-identical results across separate process runs.
